raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 30 years. My 6 mu in Quzhou is all I have, and my wife and I eat and live from what it gives us. I know every corner of this plot. 

For wheat, I will rotary till the field after the maize comes off, then sow my usual improved wheat seed in October. I have learned that this soil needs feeding, so I will spread compound fertilizer before sowing and topdress urea at the jointing stage in spring. Water is precious, but my well can manage three good irrigations: one before winter to help the seedlings survive the cold, one at green-up jointing when the wheat is hungry, and one at heading to fill the grains. I will spray twice for pesticides—once for weeds and once for the insects and fungus that come when it warms up. If the weather is fair, I expect about 550 jin per mu, maybe a bit more.

For maize, timing is everything. As soon as the wheat is out in early June, I must get the summer maize in fast before the heat dries the soil. I will plant hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage to save moisture and time. I will put fertilizer down at sowing and maybe another round when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations should be enough—one when the stalks are growing fast, and one when the tassels and silks appear. Two pesticide sprays, herbicide and one for corn borer. Hybrid maize usually gives me around 600 jin per mu in a normal year.
